transcript:
Header:
- Date/Time: 2026-12-27 14:00 UTC
- Duration: 47 min
- Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Sam (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Beacon Eng), Priya (Beacon PM), Leo (Beacon Security)
- Recording: auto

[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda: sync on the SDK invoke patterns you ran this week, go over the serialization/regression you hit with function calling, and agree next steps for liveness/kv cache experiments.
[00:18] Priya (PM): yeah thanks, we've got about three flows we want to stabilize—invoice parsing, chat-to-action, and metadata enrichment. the invoice flow is the one showing the most flakiness.
[00:34] Jordan (Eng): uh hi, yea hi. so we saw that when the model falls back from the primary large model to the smaller fallback it sometimes emits malformed JSON from the structured outputs. it's like a trailing comma or sometimes missing closing braces.
[00:50] Maya (SE): ok interesting, that matches an edge we've seen when the output gets truncated mid-token and the JSON schema enforcement on the client side chokes. can you share an example?
[01:03] Jordan (Eng): i uploaded two examples to the shared drive link in the chat — one shows a truncated array, the other shows a function call where the arguments field is null instead of an empty object.
[01:18] Alex (AE): saw those. quick question: are you running with our SDK's strict schema validator or your own post-processor?
[01:28] Jordan (Eng): we started with your SDK validator but moved it to a lighter custom validator because of latency concerns, and then we added a retry/repair pass which is slow.
[01:40] Priya (PM): latencies are critical for this flow, so we removed some checks, but clearly we lost some robustness.
[01:47] Maya (SE): ok. two interlinked issues: 1) when fallback happens the sequence length and tokenization shift can cause mid-token truncation; 2) the SDK has an escape-hatch option that returns the raw stream and a parse attempt helper. i think we need to test the escape-hatch plus a quick checksum/repair routine before the client validator.
[02:05] Leo (Security): from a security perspective, i want to make sure any repair routine doesn't reintroduce PII or change content semantics. also need to know where logs are stored and retention policy — SOC2 scope.
[02:20] Sam (CSM): noted — Alex, can we confirm where the logs for the sandbox run live and what the retention is?
[02:26] Alex (AE): yes, for the trial sandbox logs are in the tenant bucket with 30-day retention by default. for dedicated/private we can align retention and KMS. Maya will share the security doc link.
[02:38] Maya (SE): link in chat — redwood security brief v1.2. it covers KMS integration, HSM optionality, audit logs and redaction tools.
[02:50] Priya (PM): thanks. back to serialization: would enabling the KV cache reduce these truncations? our understanding is cache reduces variability by reusing prefix KV, but I'm not 100% sure.
[03:06] Maya (SE): good question. KV cache reduces repeated token generation cost and stabilizes latencies, but cache doesn't directly prevent truncation if the model switches mid-request. it can reduce the chance because repeated prefixes are cached, lowering the need to switch variants due to latency SLOs. however if you see fallback triggered by throughput constraints, that's a routing issue not KV cache.
[03:28] Jordan (Eng): in our run we toggled batching aggressively to save tokens — large batches caused spikes and then automatic fallback to the cheaper region/model. could be the root cause.
[03:42] Alex (AE): ok so we have a hypothesis: batching + model variant routing => fallback => mid-response truncation => malformed structured output.
[03:53] Priya (PM): that sounds right. what experiments do you recommend?
[03:58] Maya (SE): three experiments: A) run the same flows with batching reduced to minimal and KV cache off, B) run with batching low but with KV cache on, C) run with same load but pin to a dedicated model variant (no automatic fallback). capture token-level logs and the stream events.
[04:15] Jordan (Eng): timeline? we'd like results before the end of the quarter.
[04:19] Alex (AE): we can provision a dedicated sandbox for you for a week and run A/B/C. Maya can set it up by end of this week.
[04:27] Maya (SE): yes I'll provision the sandbox and a small dedicated pool for the pinned experiment. also will include a toggle to enable the SDK "escape_hatch_parse" flag so you get the raw stream and the helper parser.
[04:39] Leo (Security): i want to confirm the pinned pool — what level of isolation is that? VPC? encrypted at rest?
[04:46] Maya (SE): for the sandbox it will be tenant-isolated with SSE-KMS. for private we can do VPC + BYOK/HSM. i'll add the exact config in the security doc.
[04:58] Jordan (Eng): also, the function calling behavior — when the model decides to call our tool it sometimes includes arguments that reference fields we don't have. is there a way to constrain the function schema the model can use?
[05:10] Maya (SE): yes, our SDK allows you to register a strict function schema and to validate arguments server-side before invoking your tool. there's also a mode to reject out-of-schema calls and return a structured error rather than attempting silent correction.
[05:22] Alex (AE): does that help with your repair pass being slower?
[05:25] Jordan (Eng): potentially, if the SDK rejects and gives a clear error we can avoid the slow repair fallback. but we worry about user-visible errors.
[05:33] Priya (PM): maybe a hybrid: reject in canary, accept+repair in production until repaired, or use a canary/pinned policy.
[05:40] Maya (SE): exactly — we support rollout policies. you can do canary 5% pinned to the strict schema, monitor errors, then expand. the console exposes per-route error rates and token breakdown.
[05:52] Jordan (Eng): what's the expected latency hit for strict schema validation server-side? we need numbers.
[05:57] Maya (SE): small, usually single-digit ms for argument schema validation. the bigger hit is network roundtrips if you add extra verification calls.
[06:05] Alex (AE): we'll include an approximate latency delta in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[06:10] Priya (PM): on metrics: we want SLA targets —  p95 < 350ms for chat routes and p95 < 600ms for invoice flow. is that realistic?
[06:21] Maya (SE): p95 600ms for invoice depends on model size and token length; with a dedicated pool and batching tuned we can approach that. for p95 350ms for chat you likely need a smaller low-latency variant pinned.
[06:33] Jordan (Eng): also, cost tradeoffs — our finance team asks about per-invocation delta if we pin to dedicated versus letting routing pick cheaper variants.
[06:42] Alex (AE): we'll provide a cost delta table for the expected daily volume — that's one of the action items.
[06:49] Priya (PM): are there any quick SDK snippets we can use to try strict function schemas?
[06:56] Maya (SE): yes, i'll drop node/python examples in the shared folder — they'll show register_function_schema, escape_hatch_parse, and the validator hook.
[07:06] Sam (CSM): i put the shared folder link in the chat.
[07:10] Jordan (Eng): thanks. one more point — telemetry. when we run the liveness tests, what telemetry should we capture?
[07:18] Maya (SE): capture model_variant, batch_size, token_count, stream_events (open/close/truncate), fallback_reason, and per-token latency if possible. include the SDK logs with parse attempts and validator results.
[07:31] Priya (PM): perfect. we'll also redact PII before sharing.
[07:35] Leo (Security): confirm encryption in transit and at rest for logs and that KMS keys can be customer-managed for private.
[07:43] Maya (SE): confirmed. i'll note this in the security doc and list BYOK/HSM options.
[07:49] Alex (AE): ok let's recap next steps — Maya will provision sandboxes and upload SDK snippets; Alex will send benchmark spreadsheet and pricing delta; Jordan will run experiments A/B/C and share logs; Leo will send SOC2 scoping.
[08:05] Priya (PM): and we'll reconvene after you have the runs, say Jan 11?
[08:13] Sam (CSM): Jan 11 works for us. i'll send the calendar invite now.
[08:18] Alex (AE): thanks everyone. quick note: if you hit any blocking errors use the support channel and DM Maya.
[08:25] Jordan (Eng): will do, thanks.
[08:28] Alex (AE): bye all.
